definitions.explanation: A narrative, especially a traditional or fictional one.

examples.japanese: この{物語|ものがたり}はとても{面白|おもしろ}い。
{子供|こども}に{寝|ね}る{前|まえ}に{物語|ものがたり}を{読|よ}んであげた。
examples.english: I read a story to the child before bed.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}は{実話|じつわ}に{基|もと}づいた{感動|かんどう}{的|てき}な{物語|ものがたり}だ。
examples.english: This movie is a moving story based on a true story.

examples.japanese: 『{源氏|げんじ}{物語|ものがたり}』は{千年|せんねん}{以上|いじょう}{前|まえ}に{書|か}かれた{作品|さくひん}だが、{今|いま}でも{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}に{読|よ}まれている。
examples.english: The Tale of Genji was written over a thousand years ago, but it is still read by many people today.

notes:
{物語|ものがたり} means a tale, story, or narrative. It has a literary and somewhat elevated tone compared to {話|はなし} (story, talk).

ETYMOLOGY:
{物|もの} (thing) + {語|かた}り (telling), from the verb {語|かた}る (to tell, to narrate).

FAMOUS WORKS:
- {源氏|げんじ}{物語|ものがたり}: The Tale of Genji
- {竹取|たけとり}{物語|ものがたり}: The Tale of the Bamboo Cutter
- {平家|へいけ}{物語|ものがたり}: The Tale of the Heike

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {物語|ものがたり}を{語|かた}る: to tell a story
- {物語|ものがたり}が{展開|てんかい}する: a story unfolds
- ～{物語|ものがたり}: a tale of ~ (used in titles)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {話|はなし}: story, talk (casual, everyday)
- {物語|ものがたり}: tale, narrative (literary, structured)
- {小説|しょうせつ}: novel (specifically published fiction)
